summary: BULB Air is an interactive, browser-based 3D geospatial and statistical trend-verification platform developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge (Be An Earth System Trend Detective!). Focusing on Uzbekistan from 2004 to 2026, BULB Air maps six Earth system variables—Composite Index, NO₂, PM2.5, MODIS AOD/Dust, Black Carbon/SO₂, and CSA SWOT/RCM water deficit—across ~280 3D extruded prisms over real DEM terrain and 14 administrative regions. To address the challenge of identifying where, how much, and how significantly environmental variables change, the platform cross-examines three independent data streams ("witnesses"): orbital satellites (NASA OMI/TROPOMI, MODIS, CSA SWOT), MERRA-2 reanalysis, and NOAA ISD/UzHydromet ground stations. It computes Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) slopes with 95% confidence intervals, residuals, Mann-Kendall significance tests, and Theil-Sen median slopes, while accounting for winter cloud and fog obscuration. By separating true long-term trends from seasonal inversions and dust cycles, BULB Air provides transparent, scientifically grounded environmental intelligence in both English and Russian.

[15.11.2026 11:56] Иброхим ихт: WHAT DOES IT DO & HOW DOES IT WORK?
BULB Air is a browser-based 3D Earth observation and trend-analysis web app for Uzbekistan covering 2004–2026 (with an optional 2015–2026 filter)[cite: 1]. Using a 135-vertex GeoJSON border and a point-in-polygon algorithm, it renders ~280 3D extruded prisms over real Terrarium DEM terrain across all 14 regions of Uzbekistan[cite: 1].

Users can explore 6 environmental indicators from NASA, NOAA, and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) sources[cite: 1]:
- Composite Index (idx): Combined multi-source environmental score[cite: 1].
- NO₂ (×10¹⁵ molec/cm²): NASA Aura OMI / Sentinel-5P TROPOMI tropospheric column[cite: 1].
- PM2.5 (µg/m³): NASA MERRA-2 aerosol reanalysis calibrated with NOAA ISD ground stations[cite: 1].
- AOD / Dust (τ₅₅₀): MODIS Terra/Aqua aerosol optical depth tracking Aralkum and Kyzylkum dust[cite: 1].
- Black Carbon / SO₂ (µg/m³): MERRA-2 industrial combustion and smelter emissions[cite: 1].
- SWOT / Water Deficit (%): NASA GES DISC and CSA SWOT / RADARSAT RCM surface water and soil moisture deficit[cite: 1].

The app combines three interactive tools[cite: 1]:
1. 3D Map & Seasonal Physics: Simulates 4 seasonal modes (Winter smog inversion, Summer Aralkum dust, Spring convection, Autumn heating/calms), 5 severity levels (Optimal to Critical), timeline playback, 4 camera presets, 3 basemaps (Google Hybrid 3D, Google Maps, Dark Aerospace), and a live cursor probe showing elevation, boundary-layer height, humidity, and variable values[cite: 1].
2. 14-Region Bar Chart: Ranks all regions against WHO/reference thresholds (sortable by value, trend slope, or name) with one-click 3D fly-to navigation[cite: 1].
3. "3-Witness" Statistical Trend Detective: Compares three independent data sources—Satellite (NASA/CSA), MERRA-2 Reanalysis, and Ground Stations (NOAA ISD / UzHydromet)[cite: 1]. It calculates OLS linear regression (β₁ ± 95% confidence interval, R², Pearson r, 2027 forecast, and residuals eᵢ), Mann-Kendall significance (Z and p-value), and Theil-Sen median slopes to classify each trend as Confirmed Upward, Confirmed Decline, Witnesses Diverge, or Inconclusive[cite: 1].

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT
- Prevents False Conclusions: Requiring agreement across satellite, reanalysis, and ground data—plus statistical significance (p < 0.05 and a 95% CI that does not cross zero)—stops short-term weather cycles or winter fog from being mistaken for long-term trends[cite: 1].
- Explains Regional Differences: Shows why pollution behaves differently across Uzbekistan—contrasting winter smog trapped in mountain valleys (Tashkent, Fergana) with summer salt-dust storms from the dried Aralkum seabed (Karakalpakstan, Khorezm)[cite: 1].
- Open & Easy to Use: Runs directly in any browser without backend setup or paid API keys, with instant English/Russian (RU / EN) switching for researchers, students, and citizens[cite: 1].

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED
- Languages & Formats: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), GeoJSON, and SVG[cite: 1].
- Libraries & UI: MapLibre GL JS v4.7.1 (WebGL2 3D terrain and fill-extrusion), Tailwind CSS, and Google Fonts (Inter, JetBrains Mono)[cite: 1].
- Map & Elevation Tiles: AWS S3 Terrarium DEM, Google Hybrid/Maps raster tiles, and CARTO Dark Matter tiles[cite: 1].
- Scientific Datasets & Methods: NASA Giovanni & AppEEARS (OMI, TROPOMI, MODIS), NASA GES DISC (MERRA-2, GLDAS), CSA SWOT & RADARSAT RCM, NOAA NCEI ISD & UzHydromet stations, and trend methods from NASA NTRS 20090042747 and KNMI Climate Explorer[cite: 1].
[15.11.2026 11:56] Иброхим ихт: CREATIVITY
- "3-Witness" Verification: Frames trend detection like a courtroom cross-examination where satellite, model, and ground witnesses must corroborate each other[cite: 1].
- 3D Data Prisms + Real Landmarks: Combines 3D data cubes with 10 3D architectural and industrial landmarks (such as the Almalyk Smelter, Syrdarya TPP, Tashkent TV Tower, Registan, and Muynak Aral Sea Lighthouse) to connect emission sources and geography with environmental data[cite: 1].
- Clear-Sky Honesty Bar & Clean View: Explicitly displays when winter clouds/fog block satellite sensors and includes an H-key Clean View mode for distraction-free 3D exploration[cite: 1].

FACTORS CONSIDERED BY OUR TEAM
- Topography & Weather: Modeled how mountain basins trap winter pollutants under shallow boundary layers (~420 m), while desert plains drive summer convection (~1,850 m) and dust uplift[cite: 1].
- Satellite Cloud Limits: Accounted for lower winter clear-sky visibility (36–45%) caused by fog and clouds, relying more on MERRA-2 and ground stations in winter[cite: 1].
- Statistical Reliability & Clean Baseline: Paired OLS regression with non-parametric Mann-Kendall and Theil-Sen tests, and included high-altitude Jizzakh/Zaamin (1,180 m) as a clean-air reference[cite: 1].
